question: Which tool does a nurse grab to take a look inside a patient's ear canal and ear drum?
explanation: Spot on! An otoscope has a handy built-in light and magnifier so you can easily check the ear canal and tympanic membrane.

question: When checking an adult's ear with an otoscope, how should you pull the outer ear (pinna)?
explanation: You've got it! Pulling the adult pinna up and back straightens out the curved ear canal so you get a clear view of the eardrum.

question: What is the main underlying issue in a patient with glaucoma?
explanation: Exactly! Glaucoma happens when pressure builds up inside the eye, which can slowly put the squeeze on the optic nerve.

question: A patient just had cataract surgery and is getting ready to go home. What is a key instruction to give them?

options.A: Wash your face vigorously with antibacterial soap daily
options.B: Sleep flat on your back without using any pillows
options.C: Avoid heavy lifting and straining during bowel movements
options.D: Keep the affected eye uncovered at all times

explanation: Spot on! Straining or heavy lifting ramps up the pressure inside the eye, which is the last thing you want right after eye surgery.

question: What three main symptoms usually point toward Meniere's disease?

options.B: Fever, ear pain, and purulent drainage

explanation: Correct! Meniere's is linked to inner ear fluid trouble, bringing on sudden dizziness (vertigo), ringing in the ears (tinnitus), and hearing changes.

question: Why do young children get middle ear infections so much easier than adults?

options.A: Their tympanic membranes are thinner and easily ruptured
options.B: Their Eustachian tubes are shorter and more horizontal
options.C: They lack antibodies in their outer ear canals
options.D: They produce excessive earwax that traps bacteria

explanation: Well done! Because kids' Eustachian tubes lie flatter and shorter, germs and fluid slip easily from the throat right into the middle ear.

question: What is the best first step when a patient suddenly has a bloody nose?

options.A: Instruct the client to blow the nose hard to clear out clots
options.B: Pack both nasal cavities tightly with dry gauze strips immediately
options.C: Place the client flat on their back and tilt the head backward
options.D: Have the client sit upright and lean forward while pinching the soft nose

explanation: You nailed it! Leaning forward keeps blood out of the throat, and pinching the soft part of the nose puts direct pressure right where it's bleeding.

question: What happens if a patient uses over-the-counter medicated nasal sprays for too many days in a row?

options.D: Permanent loss of the sense of smell

explanation: Exactly! Overusing these sprays causes the blood vessels in the nose to swell right back up even worse once the drug wears off.

question: What is often the very first sign that a patient is bleeding after having their tonsils out?
explanation: Spot on! Since blood pools quietly in the back of the throat after surgery, swallowing a lot is usually your early clue before any throwing up happens.

question: Which drink should you avoid giving a child right after a tonsillectomy?
explanation: You got it! Stay away from red drinks because if the patient throws up, the red color looks just like fresh blood and causes unnecessary panic.

question: Why should you gently press the inner corner of the eye right after putting in eye drops?

options.A: To help the liquid medication spread evenly across the entire surface of the cornea
options.B: To prevent the medication from entering the tear duct and causing systemic side effects
options.C: To stimulate tear production and wash away any excess debris in the eye socket
options.D: To seal the eyelids shut and prevent the client from blinking too rapidly

explanation: Brilliant! This little trick (nasolacrimal occlusion) stops the medicine from draining into the nose where it could get absorbed into the rest of the body.

question: What is the proper way to position an adult's ear before putting in ear drops?

options.A: Pull the pinna up and back before instilling the drops
options.B: Keep the client sitting upright for thirty minutes after
options.C: Insert the dropper tip firmly deep into the ear canal
options.D: Pull the earlobe straight down before putting in drops

explanation: Correct! Pulling the pinna up and back opens up the canal so the drops slide right down nicely toward the eardrum.

question: What is the best way to walk down the hall with a patient who has a visual impairment?

options.A: Walk behind the client and verbally give step-by-step directions
options.B: Walk side by side while holding hands tightly with the client
options.C: Push the client from behind by placing hands firmly on their shoulders
options.D: Walk slightly ahead and let the client hold onto your elbow

explanation: You've got it! Letting them hold your elbow while you lead slightly gives them physical cues for your movements and keeps them feeling secure.

question: What is the most helpful way to talk with a patient who has significant hearing loss?

options.A: Shout loudly directly into the client's ear canal so they can hear
options.B: Face the client directly and speak in a normal tone without shouting
options.C: Speak very quickly using complex medical terminology for accuracy
options.D: Turn off all lights in the room to help the client concentrate better

explanation: Spot on! Facing them lets them read your lips and see expressions, and keeping a normal volume prevents distorting your voice.
